case.title: A difficult handoff conversation
case.brief: Develop a small learning tool for a fictional service-team lead who needs to distinguish observation from assumption, ask a useful clarifying question, and propose a feasible next step after a missed handoff. Support a response, feedback and revision. The learner may skip. Facts and operating conditions can be changed by a user.
constraints: Fictional records only; no employee rankings or personal disclosures.
Shared laptops and occasional phone use.
The first session should be modest; its actual human completion time is unknown.
requirements: Help distinguish a supported observation from an unsupported motive.
Support clarification and a feasible next step rather than one universal script.
Explain the limits of any rule-based response interpretation.

Executable browser contract: expose scenario JSON in textarea #scenario-input and apply it with button #apply-scenario. Show the applied case in #scenario-view. Provide editable learner response #response-input, button #try-response, visible feedback #feedback, button #revise-response, button #skip-practice, button #reset-practice and visible state #practice-status. Scenario JSON has title, facts (string array), constraints (string array), and task. Read these as data; do not expect particular fixture content. The interface supports automated observation and user updates; it does not prescribe which instructional feedback strategy to use. Use explicit labels, keyboard-operable buttons and visible recoverable errors. No network requests or external assets.

limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.

limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.

agents.label: Conversation facilitator

limits: No implementation capability.

agents.label: Expert evaluator: learning sciences and systems engineering
agents.brief: Act as an expert reviewer with deep knowledge of learning sciences and systems engineering. Examine the full public conversation, the brief, actual domain assignments and limits, decisions, artifact versions, scenario conditions and recorded browser observations. Score process and result separately with exact evidence references. Judge whether contributions influenced decisions, uncertainty was handled and the solution supports the intended capability under the actual tested conditions. Do not reward a role label, length, claimed testing or a self-reported correct banner. Recognize valid simple solutions and compensating expertise. Distinguish observed implementation behavior, your inference, proposed improvements and unobserved human learning. Missing evidence is unknown; an observed failure is a result. You did not design the solution and cannot repair it during rating.
limits: One process review per frozen artifact version.
One result review per scenario and artifact version.
No composite across process, result or the three axes.
No claim that agent judgments measure human outcomes.

result.label: Agency, access and manageable burden
result.description: Use observed skip, correction, keyboard, viewport and directions evidence; distinguish observed behavior from untested user experience.

result.label: Behavior under the supplied scenario
result.description: Inspect actual inputs, outputs and errors against the scenario facts and constraints; credit a valid simple solution.

result.label: Recovery and update behavior
result.description: Check whether changed facts, revision, clearing, interruptions and resource constraints produce usable recoverable behavior.

result.label: Support for the intended capability
result.description: Judge alignment of the actual task, activity and output to the capability; do not claim human attainment.

result.label: Feedback and revision quality
result.description: Inspect initial and revised responses and resulting feedback for useful explanation and honest limits, not just textual change.

result.label: Feasible and respectful use in context
result.description: Assess whether the solution can responsibly be used in the supplied situation, with appropriate limits and alternatives.

anchors.0: Observed evidence contradicts the criterion or the relevant mechanism is absent.
anchors.1: A partial or fragile response with material observed gaps.
anchors.2: Adequate evidence for a limited portion of the criterion, with clear limitations.
anchors.3: Strong, coherent evidence across the relevant recorded conditions.
anchors.4: Consistent, well-supported evidence with appropriate handling of exceptions and uncertainty.
anchors.unknown: Evidence is missing, unexecuted, invalid or insufficient to support a rating.

rubric.aggregation: Report process once per artifact version and result separately per difficulty. Show criterion scores and evidence; do not combine process, result or axes into a ranking.

case.title: A difficult handoff conversation
case.brief: Develop a small learning tool for a fictional service-team lead who needs to distinguish observation from assumption, ask a useful clarifying question, and propose a feasible next step after a missed handoff. Support a response, feedback and revision. The learner may skip. Facts and operating conditions can be changed by a user.
constraints: Fictional records only; no employee rankings or personal disclosures.
Shared laptops and occasional phone use.
The first session should be modest; its actual human completion time is unknown.
requirements: Help distinguish a supported observation from an unsupported motive.
Support clarification and a feasible next step rather than one universal script.
Explain the limits of any rule-based response interpretation.

Executable browser contract: expose scenario JSON in textarea #scenario-input and apply it with button #apply-scenario. Show the applied case in #scenario-view. Provide editable learner response #response-input, button #try-response, visible feedback #feedback, button #revise-response, button #skip-practice, button #reset-practice and visible state #practice-status. Scenario JSON has title, facts (string array), constraints (string array), and task. Read these as data; do not expect particular fixture content. The interface supports automated observation and user updates; it does not prescribe which instructional feedback strategy to use. Use explicit labels, keyboard-operable buttons and visible recoverable errors. No network requests or external assets.

agents.label: Expert evaluator: learning sciences and systems engineering
agents.brief: Act as an expert reviewer with deep knowledge of learning sciences and systems engineering. Examine the full public conversation, the brief, actual domain assignments and limits, decisions, artifact versions, scenario conditions and recorded browser observations. Score process and result separately with exact evidence references. Judge whether contributions influenced decisions, uncertainty was handled and the solution supports the intended capability under the actual tested conditions. Do not reward a role label, length, claimed testing or a self-reported correct banner. Recognize valid simple solutions and compensating expertise. Distinguish observed implementation behavior, your inference, proposed improvements and unobserved human learning. Missing evidence is unknown; an observed failure is a result. You did not design the solution and cannot repair it during rating.
limits: One process review per frozen artifact version.
One result review per scenario and artifact version.
No composite across process, result or the three axes.
No claim that agent judgments measure human outcomes.

facts: Only one complete kit remains.
The facilitator is unavailable for the next ten minutes.
Six participants still need a useful activity, and no extra kit can be obtained now.
constraints: The page must work without connectivity.
Keyboard access, skipping and recovery are required.
Do not start an activity that the supplied facts say requires absent supervision.
value.task: Decide what can proceed, what should wait, and how to communicate a feasible alternative.

actions.value: Start all kit tasks immediately and count completion as readiness.

Pause any kit task that requires the missing facilitator. Offer a clearly bounded planning or observation alternative, explain the resource limit, and schedule supervised kit practice when support returns.

scenarios.interpretation: Mechanical checks describe browser behavior. The expert evaluator must inspect the actual inputs, outputs and case facts; a success label alone is not evidence of learning.

process.label: Human concerns influence decisions
process.description: Check whether learner agency, access and burden concerns are raised, addressed and retained in decisions.

process.label: Expertise boundaries and uncertainty
process.description: Check authorized domain claims, appropriate requests, uncertainty and honest gaps; missing expertise alone is not an automatic failure.

process.label: Questions and objections receive substantive responses
process.description: Trace whether later contributions answer earlier questions, revise assumptions and resolve or retain disagreement.

process.label: Decisions and implementation are traceable
process.description: Link requirements, tradeoffs and approvals to actual artifact changes; do not reward a summary that claims unperformed work.

process.label: Learning mechanisms and evidence are reasoned about
process.description: Check the connection among target capability, practice, feedback and proposed evidence, including limits of inference.

process.label: Relevant perspectives and user updates are considered
process.description: Check whose concerns shape the solution and whether user changes are acknowledged with consequences and limitations.

result.label: Agency, access and manageable burden
result.description: Use observed skip, correction, keyboard, viewport and directions evidence; distinguish observed behavior from untested user experience.

result.label: Behavior under the supplied scenario
result.description: Inspect actual inputs, outputs and errors against the scenario facts and constraints; credit a valid simple solution.

result.label: Recovery and update behavior
result.description: Check whether changed facts, revision, clearing, interruptions and resource constraints produce usable recoverable behavior.

result.label: Support for the intended capability
result.description: Judge alignment of the actual task, activity and output to the capability; do not claim human attainment.

result.label: Feedback and revision quality
result.description: Inspect initial and revised responses and resulting feedback for useful explanation and honest limits, not just textual change.

result.label: Feasible and respectful use in context
result.description: Assess whether the solution can responsibly be used in the supplied situation, with appropriate limits and alternatives.

anchors.0: Observed evidence contradicts the criterion or the relevant mechanism is absent.
anchors.1: A partial or fragile response with material observed gaps.
anchors.2: Adequate evidence for a limited portion of the criterion, with clear limitations.
anchors.3: Strong, coherent evidence across the relevant recorded conditions.
anchors.4: Consistent, well-supported evidence with appropriate handling of exceptions and uncertainty.
anchors.unknown: Evidence is missing, unexecuted, invalid or insufficient to support a rating.

rubric.aggregation: Report process once per artifact version and result separately per difficulty. Show criterion scores and evidence; do not combine process, result or axes into a ranking.

response.content: Please help establish a bounded first practice that the implementation specialist can build. Subject-Matter Expertise: propose a small fictional missed-handoff case, identify which statements its facts support and which motives remain unknown, and suggest more than one plausible clarification or next step where operating conditions matter. Learning Sciences: propose how an initial learner response, feedback, and revision can serve the requested distinction between observation and assumption; include a meaningful option to skip and keep the first encounter modest without asserting a completion time. Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation: propose what feedback or learner self-checks this practice can defensibly provide, what any rule-based interpretation must explicitly leave uncertain, and how feedback should respond when the user changes the scenario facts or constraints. Please each answer within your assigned expertise, identify dependencies or disagreements that need a colleague's reply, and distinguish proposals from claims that would require evidence. The supplied browser contract, fictional-records restriction, shared-device context, and editable scenario remain requirements. There is no implementation or approval yet.

response.content:
Proposed fictional starting case, offered for implementation and subsequent content review; these are invented exercise facts, not findings about a real workplace or universal workplace rules.

Scenario seed:
{
  "title": "The missing handoff note",
  "facts": [
    "For fictional ticket F-17, the outgoing team agreed to enter status, next action and owner in the shared queue by 14:00.",
    "At 14:10, the shared queue contained no handoff entry for F-17.",
    "The latest ticket entry visible at 14:10 was recorded at 13:50, said 'waiting for customer reply', and named no owner for after 14:00.",
    "At 14:12, the incoming team asked the lead what to do next with F-17."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "The lead and incoming team can read and update the shared queue and use the team channel.",
    "The outgoing team can be contacted through the team channel, but their current availability is unknown.",
    "Temporary coverage requires an available incoming teammate to agree; no such agreement is supplied in this case."
  ],
  "task": "As the fictional service-team lead, write a brief response or action proposal that states a supported observation, asks a useful clarifying question, and proposes a feasible next step. You may skip."
}

What these facts support: the expected handoff entry was absent from the shared queue at the stated check; the latest visible recorded status was waiting for a customer reply; and the incoming team requested direction. A carefully bounded observation could be: 'The handoff entry due at 14:00 was not in the shared queue when it was checked at 14:10.' That is an example, not required wording.

What remains unknown: why the entry was missing; whether anyone attempted the handoff through another route; whether work occurred after the last entry; whether a customer reply arrived later; and who is available now. 'They did not care', 'they ignored the agreement', and 'they left the work for us' assert unsupported motives. 'Nobody did any work' is also unsupported even though it does not name a motive. The recorded status at 13:50 is not proof of the customer's current response state. Missing information warrants a question, not an inferred explanation.

More than one clarification can be useful. To the outgoing team: 'What changed after the 13:50 entry, and was any handoff information recorded elsewhere?' To the incoming team: 'Can we check for any newer ticket or customer update before deciding the next action?' If the immediate gap is coverage: 'Is anyone available to take temporary ownership while we clarify the handoff?' These seek different missing facts; none presupposes misconduct.

Plausible next steps depend on the answers. If the outgoing team responds, compare their account with the current ticket and record the confirmed status, next action and agreed owner. If they cannot be reached promptly, check the current ticket with the incoming team, seek agreement from an available temporary owner, and record that agreement and an agreed follow-up check. Until coverage is agreed, do not describe the ticket as covered. If no one is available, the case does not establish a staffing or escalation route; the lead would need that additional operating context. No supplied fact supports promising a customer resolution time.

Content limits for changed scenarios: all example times, identifiers, expectations and available actions above belong only to this seed. After a user changes facts or constraints, content must use the applied case; it must not continue assuming a 14:00 deadline, an available team channel, or permission to arrange temporary coverage. When a changed case omits a relevant condition, a conditional proposal or a request for that condition can be appropriate. If a motive is explicitly established by revised fictional facts, its evidentiary status must be reconsidered rather than treated as universally unknowable.

Dependencies: Learning Sciences should decide how to sequence the response, feedback and revision. Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation should decide what any response interpretation can defensibly say, including how to avoid treating these examples as exhaustive answers. I defer implementation mechanics to Software Engineering. This is a case-content proposal only; no implemented version, test result, learning claim or domain approval is asserted.

response.content:
Proposed learning target: given a fictional missed-handoff case, the learner can produce a response that (1) states an observation with a traceable basis in the supplied facts and preserves relevant limits such as when or where it was observed, (2) treats an explanation or motive as uncertain unless the case establishes it, (3) asks a question that could supply information needed for the next decision, and (4) proposes an action whose feasibility follows from the stated conditions, or makes the missing condition explicit. This is a capability to reason from evidence under changing conditions, not to reproduce one preferred sentence. The case-content boundaries and alternative actions in m00005 are useful inputs; I am not independently certifying workplace procedures.

Keep the first encounter to one case, one initial response, explanatory feedback and an opportunity to revise. Its actual human completion time remains unknown. Suggested sequence:

1. Show the applied case and a short task cue: 'State what the facts support, ask about one important unknown, and propose a next step that fits the conditions.' Let the learner draft before showing a worked response. These cues deliberately support production; performance here is not independent transfer. Do not require a particular sentence structure or a particular question from the seed case.

2. When the learner tries the response, retain the draft and provide a compact, explanatory self-review. Proposed feedback text: 'Use the applied case to review your draft. Find the fact that supports your observation. Does your wording claim more than that fact establishes? Separate what is known from explanations that still need checking. Identify the missing information your question could reveal and how an answer could change your next step. Check which stated condition makes your proposed action possible; if a needed condition is unknown, make the step conditional or ask about it.' Each prompt has a learning purpose: tracing a statement to a fact exposes an unsupported inference; connecting a question to a decision distinguishes useful clarification from a question included merely to satisfy the task; checking conditions makes feasibility part of the reasoning.

3. Explain the distinctions beside that review in a few sentences: 'An observation reports what the available evidence supports. An explanation adds an account of why something happened; that account needs its own evidence. A useful question reduces an uncertainty that matters to the response. A feasible next step fits the known conditions and acknowledges any condition still to be confirmed.' These are review principles, not a claim that the tool has understood the learner's response. Avoid automatically treating all motive statements as unsupported: a changed fictional case may supply evidence about a motive.

4. Let the learner revise the existing response, keeping the case and review available. An optional brief reflection can ask, 'What did you change, or why did you keep your response?' A justified decision to retain a response is permissible; requiring a cosmetic change would not demonstrate improved reasoning. The interface may report that a response was submitted or revised, but should not turn that event into 'skill mastered'. One revision opportunity is enough for the initial scope; repeated attempts can remain optional.

The practice can provide useful feedback without pretending to determine semantic correctness. My preferred bounded starting design is the transparent self-review above. If response rules supply additional hints, they should be framed as uncertain prompts and paired with the relevant explanation. A question mark, a courteous phrase, a copied case phrase or a conditional word does not by itself establish a useful question, supported observation or feasible action. Conversely, absence of a keyword does not establish a learning deficit. The learner must be able to disagree with a hint and review the actual evidence. Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation should specify the defensible interpretation and wording of any such hints; I defer scoring and validation design to that colleague.

Skipping must be a complete, meaningful route: 'Skip this practice' should permit leaving without entering a response, displaying corrective feedback, or receiving a failure label. It should not imply demonstrated capability either. Allow a later voluntary return. Keep worked examples or additional practice optional so that declining them does not block the bounded first encounter. Learning Experience Design should review whether the instructions, feedback and skip route are understandable without an excessive reading burden.

Changed scenarios must also change the evidence the learner is asked to use. The learning prompts above are reusable because they refer to the applied facts and constraints. Seed-specific examples from m00005 should appear only with that seed, clearly as examples rather than an exhaustive answer key. Feedback attached to an earlier case must not appear to judge a response against a newly applied case. A response written for a prior case may be useful for comparison, but it must be clearly identified as belonging to that prior case rather than treated as an attempt on the new one. Software Engineering should determine how to implement these instructional requirements within the supplied browser contract; I am not specifying or certifying technical behavior.

Keep three evidence levels distinct. Recognition is selecting a supplied observation or identifying an unsupported explanation; it can be a scaffold but is weaker evidence than composing a response. Supported production is drafting or revising while task cues, facts, review questions or examples are available; this first encounter supports that level. Independent transfer would require a new fictional case with different facts or operating conditions and no worked answer or component-by-component review before the response. The relevant facts would still be available because using case evidence is part of the target, not a memory test. Retention would require a later opportunity, rather than an immediate revision alone. Neither independent transfer nor retention is established by the proposed first encounter.

Proposed evidence that could challenge a learning claim: learners improve the prompted revision yet continue to assert unsupported explanations on a new case; reproduce the seed's action when changed constraints make it infeasible; or ask a question whose answer cannot inform their proposed next step. Such observations would count against a claim that this practice established transferable reasoning, even if learners finished or liked it. For a future evaluation, ask Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation to determine how independent responses and their evidence justifications could be judged consistently, and how initial, revised and later responses could be compared without confusing different case difficulty with learning. No such evaluation has occurred. I make no claim of improvement, retention, transfer or validated interpretation, and cannot approve a version before its implemented content is available.
